Navigation designed around experience, not efficiency.
What if navigation optimised for quality, not just speed? |This web app reimagines walking as an experience with routing for safety, discovery, and human-ness.

## The Question

Every navigation app solves the same problem: getting you there fast. (re)Route solves a different one — making the walk worth taking.

## How It Works

You open the app. You type what you actually want: "calm 20 min walk," "artsy date in Born," "take me to Park Güell but make it scenic," or just "surprise me." A single AI call interprets your words — not as a search query, but as an intent — and builds a walk around it.

### Three Entry Points, Three Mindsets

**GO** — destination search with route options that explain *why* each route is different, not just how long it takes.

**EXPLORE** — type a vibe, the AI curates an experience. From a themed architecture trail to a multi-stop evening out.

**WANDER** — a compass, curated pins around you, and nothing else. No route. No destination. Just direction.

## The Data Underneath

119,000 Barcelona street segments scored across noise, greenery, cleanliness, cultural richness, and safety. When you ask for "calm," the system knows which streets are actually quiet. After dark, every route automatically shifts to well-lit, active streets. Safety isn't a mode. It's a baseline.

## Smart Discovery

Ask for "artsy date" and the system reasons about what the query implies — experimental galleries, design bookshops, natural wine bars with art on the walls — then verifies every suggestion against real place data before showing it.

## Curated Layer

386 hand-curated points of interest. Themed walks spanning Gaudí, Gothic Barcelona, modernisme, hidden courtyards, public art, rooftop views, Roman ruins. A bloom calendar tracks 8 flowering species by month.

## The Research

8 in-depth interviews. 89% of survey respondents already vary their routes to explore. The tools just haven't caught up.

## What This Is

A master's thesis prototype — working proof that navigation can be designed around experience, not just efficiency. Built for Barcelona. Designed for any city worth walking.

Trip planning that looks as good as the trip.
A planning tool that thinks like an editor.|This online builder turns trip itineraries into interactive editorials.

## The Problem

Trip planning tools are either ugly spreadsheets or rigid templates. I wanted something useful for planning — editable, data-connected — that also looks like something you'd want to look at.

## What It Does

A 15-day Europe Alps Tour planned and displayed in an editorial layout inspired by travel magazines. Click-to-edit everything. Live weather per destination. Built-in image search. Asymmetric photo galleries.

## Design Approach

The layout reproduces a Keynote presentation I designed — city intro slides with split typography, day pages with photo galleries and timelines, weather widgets. A planning tool that's also beautiful enough to screenshot and share.

## What I Learned

My first real frontend project built with Claude Code — I designed the visual system, wrote the data architecture and specification, then used AI-assisted development to build it. The process itself became proof of concept for how a designer-strategist can ship functional products.

Jobs board, but make it zen.
Jobs board, but make it zen.|An AI-free listing aggregator that scores roles against your profile while taking care of your mental health.

## The Problem

The job market is brutal. AI is reshaping roles, companies hire and lay off in the same quarter, and the gap between "qualified" and "callback" has never been wider. The tools designed to help — job boards, LinkedIn, recruiter inboxes — optimise for volume, not for the person searching.

## What It Does

JobHunter scrapes hundreds of sources every six hours — Arbeitnow, Remotive, Adzuna across 17 countries, 125+ RSS feeds including direct career pages. Every listing is scored against your profile on six dimensions: role fit, skills, location, salary, company size, and personal values. Hard filters remove anything that doesn't clear your basics before a job reaches your feed.

## Pip

Pip is a soft, reactive blob on the home screen. Every session, Pip checks in: how are you feeling? Anxious? The feed opens with a breathing exercise. Motivated? Pip nudges you toward top matches. Drained? Pip tells you it's okay to close the tab.

Pip is also a literal stress ball. Tap it as many times as you want — it squishes, bounces back, makes a face.

## Adjacent Roles

In a market where roles change faster than CVs, JobHunter surfaces adjacent positions — roles with significant skill overlap you could step into. Brand strategist? It might flag UX researcher roles. The goal: expand your search without diluting it.

## Design Philosophy

Streaks and XP reward effort, not outcomes. You earn points for showing up, saving a job, or applying — not for callbacks you can't control. Confetti when you apply, because that's worth celebrating regardless of what happens next.

Free to use. Self-hosted. Your data stays yours.

A game about noticing the small stuff.
A word a day. Infinite discovery.|This web app helps humans look up from their screens to discover the beauty around them through daily quests.

## The Insight

We walk past a thousand interesting things every day without seeing them.

## How It Works

A mobile web app that gives everyone in Barcelona the same single-word prompt each day — *texture*, *tiny*, or *bright*. Step outside, find it, snap a photo, drop it on a shared city map. At midnight, the map resets.

No likes, no followers, no algorithm. Just a quiet dare to look more carefully.

## The Reframing

A cracked tile becomes the answer to *pattern*. A stranger's dog becomes *soft*. The shared map turns Barcelona into a collaborative, ever-changing gallery that lives for exactly one day.

## What I Built

Research & concept. Full Figma prototypes. Next.js frontend. Supabase backend. Leaflet mapping. Deployed on Vercel, currently in beta.

## Design Philosophy

Deliberately simple. No gamification layers, no streaks, no social pressure. The constraint of one word and one day creates focus. The shared map creates connection. Anti-social media — using a phone to make you look up from it.

The city as an open world game.
The city as an open world game.|In a world of AI that steals intentionality and attention, (re)Route gives you permission to be present.

## The Evolution

(re)Route 1.0 asked: what if navigation optimised for quality, not speed? Version 2.0 goes further — what if navigation wasn't about getting somewhere at all?

## How It Works

Open the app. A deck of quest cards greets you — LIVE events happening now, a daily community challenge, a personalised quest built from your taste profile, and AI-generated local discoveries. Pick one. Walk. Snap photos. The app learns what you love.

### Quest Types

**VISIT** — Walk to real places. 3-5 locations with proximity verification at 80m. A compass ring points to the next stop.

**WANDER** — Interpretive prompts. Walk and snap photos matching a vibe. AI judges each snap with vision.

**COLLECT** — Concrete scavenger hunts. Photograph specific things (doors, tiles, dogs). Gemini vision classifies each photo.

**LIVE** — Time-sensitive, ephemeral. Real events, recurring rhythms, golden hour windows. Generated fresh, never repeated.

## Taste Memory

The app remembers. Every query, every completed quest, every photo caption feeds a taste profile — rebuilt nightly by AI into a 150-word portrait of how you explore. Tomorrow's quests reflect today's discoveries.

## The Data

372 hand-curated POIs across Barcelona. Architecture, hidden courtyards, public art, viewpoints, gardens. Plus Google Places for the rest. The system knows when to use its own taste and when to search the world.

## What's New from v1

Native app (React Native + Expo). Quest system with 4 types. Photo snaps with AI validation. Taste memory that evolves. Badge system (24 achievements + 15 collections). Community daily quests. LIVE events via web search. Push notification infrastructure.
